modelspec.checkpoint.ParameterPath.title: ParameterPath
modelspec.checkpoint.ParameterPath.description: A stable canonical parameter path such as `TinyMLP.fc1.weight` (DESIGN.md § 2.3).

modelspec.observatory.Histogram.title: Histogram
modelspec.observatory.Histogram.description: The distribution of one tensor's elements in bins, the edges taken anew from that tensor each time statistics are taken (approval-record:parameter-statistics-settlements, question 1). With min and max the tensor's smallest and largest finite element widened to Binary64, a tensor with min < max has 32 bins and the 33 edges min + (max − min) · i / 32 for i from 0 through 32, the last edge max itself; bin i counts the finite elements x with bin_edges[i] <= x < bin_edges[i+1], and the last bin also counts x = max. A tensor with min = max has one bin, edges [min, max], counting every finite element. A tensor with no finite element has no min or max, so no edge and no bin. NaN, +inf and −inf are in no bin; nan_count, positive_infinity_count and negative_infinity_count count them, so the counts and those three sum to the tensor's element count, which ESS does not state here.

bin_edges.description: The bin edges in ascending order. Edges taken between finite min and max are finite; the type keeps null for an edge that is NaN or ±inf, which Binary64 does not hold (wave observatory-1 coordinator, 2026-10-21).

counts.description: The finite elements in each bin, in edge order.

nan_count.description: The tensor's NaN elements, counted in no bin (approval-record:parameter-statistics-settlements, question 1).

positive_infinity_count.description: The tensor's +inf elements, counted in no bin (approval-record:parameter-statistics-settlements, question 1).

negative_infinity_count.description: The tensor's −inf elements, counted in no bin (approval-record:parameter-statistics-settlements, question 1).

x-ess-invariants: ((counts.count == 0 and bin_edges.count == 0) or (counts.count == 1 and bin_edges.count == 2) or (counts.count == 32 and bin_edges.count == 33))

modelspec.observatory.MetricSample.title: MetricSample
modelspec.observatory.MetricSample.description: One named metric value at a step, such as MLM accuracy (epic:training-observatory live metric charts, epic:bert-from-scratch evaluation).

value.description: The metric's value; null when it is NaN or ±inf, which Binary64 does not hold (wave observatory-1 coordinator, 2026-10-21).

modelspec.observatory.ParameterStatistic.title: ParameterStatistics
modelspec.observatory.ParameterStatistic.description: The norm and histogram of one parameter's values or gradient at a step, by its stable path (DESIGN.md § 2.3; epic:training-observatory).

norm.description: The L2 norm of the tensor, the square root of the sum of its elements' squares, each element widened to Binary64 and summed in row-major order (approval-record:parameter-statistics-settlements, question 2); null when it is NaN or ±inf, which Binary64 does not hold, as it is when an element is NaN or ±inf (wave observatory-1 coordinator, 2026-10-21).

modelspec.observatory.RunEventBody.title: RunEventBody
modelspec.observatory.RunEventBody.description: The typed event the training process sends, one per step and one per run lifecycle change (epic:training-observatory). A run is started, then finished or failed, and its stream says so, RunStarted first, then one StepCompleted per recorded loss, then exactly one of RunFinished or RunFailed, last. These are not TrainingRun lifecycle states, which keep the one state Recorded of the record, because ESS moves an entity's state only by a command outcome (ESS-ENTITY-005), and this specification declares no commands. RunFinished carries nothing; the final loss is the last StepCompleted's. A run refused before its first step, such as by E-DATA-003, sends RunStarted then RunFailed and no StepCompleted.

modelspec.observatory.RunFailed.title: RunFailed
modelspec.observatory.RunFailed.description: The event of a run failing, the last of its stream (RunEventBody). A failure is a diagnostic or a runtime error (DESIGN.md § 8.1, diagnostics distinguish user specification errors from runtime failures).

code.description: The diagnostic code that refused the run, such as E-DATA-003 (DESIGN.md § 8.1, M0 codes for `train`); absent for a runtime error, which has no code.

message.description: The failure on one line, the diagnostic's message or the runtime error as `modelspec train` reports it.

modelspec.observatory.RunStarted.title: RunStarted
modelspec.observatory.RunStarted.description: The event of a run starting, the first of its stream (RunEventBody). It carries the two TrainingRun fields that say which steps follow, start_step through start_step + steps (DESIGN.md § 6), and the TrainingRun field that says what a masked-language-model run trains on, data_binding_id; the other record fields are the run's artifact and record, which M0 does not write (story:m0-cpu-sgd-training, Out of scope).

steps.description: TrainingRun.steps, the steps of this invocation.

start_step.description: TrainingRun.start_step, the step of the first StepCompleted.

data_binding_id.description: TrainingRun.data_binding_id, the binding_id of the `binding.json` of the packed directory `modelspec train --data` trains on; absent for a run on synthetic or dense data (story:bert-train-data-binding, coordinator decision D48, 2026-10-25, `.engineering/waves/bert-1.md`).

modelspec.observatory.StatisticsSubject.title: StatisticsSubject
modelspec.observatory.StatisticsSubject.description: Whether statistics describe a parameter's values or the gradient of the loss with respect to it (epic:training-observatory parameter/gradient histograms and norms).

modelspec.observatory.StepCompleted.title: StepCompleted
modelspec.observatory.StepCompleted.description: The event of one completed training step (epic:training-observatory), one for each of the steps + 1 losses a run records, steps start_step through start_step + steps in order; step k is the loss after k updates and the last is the loss of the final parameters (DESIGN.md § 8, the `step <k> loss <v>` lines; `train::runner` in modelspec-runtime). Its loss is the loss the CLI prints for that step (DESIGN.md § 8).

step.description: The step number the run reached, as TrainingRun.current_step (DESIGN.md § 6.1 step number).

loss.description: The rank-0 loss value of the step (DESIGN.md § 2.2, § 8); null when the loss is NaN or ±inf, which Binary64 does not hold, as a diverging run records (wave observatory-1 coordinator, 2026-10-21). The CLI prints a `step <k> loss <v>` line on stdout only for step 0, every 50th step and the last step; for a printed step whose loss is null that line names which, `NaN`, `inf` or `-inf`, and for any other step nothing names it (wave observatory-1 coordinator, 2026-10-22).

metrics.description: Metric samples of the step besides the loss; names are unique.

parameters.description: Value and gradient statistics per parameter at a sampled step, empty at every other step (approval-record:parameter-statistics-settlements, question 3); the pair (path, subject) is unique, which ESS does not state here. `modelspec train --backend cpu --statistics-every N`, N at least 1 and 100 without the flag, samples step k when k is the run's start_step, a multiple of N, or start_step + steps. A sampled step lists each declared parameter in path order, its Value entry for its values after k updates, the values step k reads, then, for k < start_step + steps, its Gradient entry for the gradient of step k's loss with respect to it, the gradient step k's update applies. Step start_step + steps, the loss of the final parameters, makes no update and so has Value entries only. A parameter the loss does not read has no gradient and so no Gradient entry (DESIGN.md § 3.3 step 4). A Vulkan run keeps parameters and gradients on the device between its host waits, so `modelspec train --backend vulkan` samples only step start_step, from the values it uploads, and step start_step + steps, from the values it reads back after the last step, each with one Value entry per declared parameter in path order, the values the step reads as on the CPU, and no Gradient entry; every other step has the list empty, the statistics add no read-back and no host wait, and `--statistics-every` with `--backend vulkan` is a usage error (approval-record:parameter-statistics-settlements, question 3, "the first step also carries values" and "the final post-loop event always carries values"; story:observatory-parameter-statistics).

x-ess-invariants: distinct sample in metrics by sample.name
